primary_claim: Steering vectors optimized on a single training example generalize to mediate safety-relevant behavior across many inputs, including largely mediating harmful/benign choice in the Poser alignment-faking testbed and achieving up to 96.9% attack success rate on Harmbench for refusal suppression.

effect.value: 96.9% (best vector, Gemma-2-2B-it); 93.1% (LLaMA-3.1-8B-Instruct); vs 30.0% for prefilling-attack baseline

contradicts_or_qualifies: the creators of Poser were unable to find a steering vector that mediates harmful vs benign action using CAA trained only on good-oversight (benign) prompts, whereas this work found one using one-shot steering optimization

Turner et al.'s report found optimized steering vectors on Gemini-1.5 no longer beat prompting for increasing TruthfulQA performance, but the authors argue this does not mean steering vectors are useless in safety-relevant settings where prompting is insufficient
stated_future_work: running more experiments on steering vector optimization dynamics, including optimizing on multiple examples
further exploring steering vector loss landscape geometry
exploring alternative methods such as noisy steering (injecting noise into activations during steering optimization)
porting theoretical work on neural network learning (e.g. singular learning theory / local learning coefficient) over to the steering vector optimization setting
limitations_stated: one-shot steering isn't a 'magic bullet' that yields perfect steering vectors all the time
large variance in steering vector efficacy depending on which example the vector was trained on
evaluation of the anti-refusal steering vectors was qualitative, not quantitative, using the Harmbench classifier model
quote: our best-performing vector obtains a maximum attack success rate of 96.9% on Harmbench, after being trained on a single example.
